english: Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$. Let $N$ denote the number of subsets $S$ of $A\times A$ such that $(1,2)\notin S$ and $S=X\times Y$ for some subsets $X$ and $Y$ of $A$. Then the value of $N$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A=\{1,2,3\}$ है। माना $N$, $A\times A$ के उन उपसमुच्चयों $S$ की संख्या है जिनके लिए $(1,2)\notin S$ है तथा $A$ के किन्हीं उपसमुच्चयों $X$ तथा $Y$ हेतु $S=X\times Y$ है। तब $N$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $n(X\times Y)=n(X)\,n(Y)$, so $X\times Y=\emptyset$ iff $X=\emptyset$ or $Y=\emptyset$: all these give one subset, $\emptyset$
For non-empty $X,Y$ the set $X\times Y$ fixes $X$ (first entries) and $Y$ (second entries), so distinct pairs $(X,Y)$ give distinct subsets: $(2^{3}-1)^{2}=49$
$(1,2)\in X\times Y\iff 1\in X,\ 2\in Y$: $2^{2}\cdot2^{2}=16$ of them
solution_full: A subset of $A\times A$ of the form $X\times Y$ may arise from several pairs $(X,Y)$, so the pairs $(X,Y)$ cannot simply be counted.
Since $n(X\times Y)=n(X)\,n(Y)$, the product is empty exactly when $X=\emptyset$ or $Y=\emptyset$. All such pairs $(X,Y)$ (there are $2^{3}+2^{3}-1=15$ of them) produce the single subset $\emptyset$.

If $X\neq\emptyset$ and $Y\neq\emptyset$, then $X$ is the set of first entries of the pairs in $X\times Y$ and $Y$ is the set of second entries. So $X\times Y$ determines $X$ and $Y$, and distinct pairs of non-empty subsets give distinct products.
$A$ has $2^{3}=8$ subsets, $2^{3}-1=7$ of them non-empty, so there are $7\cdot7=49$ non-empty products. Together with $\emptyset$: $50$ subsets of $A\times A$ are of the form $X\times Y$.

Among them, $(1,2)\in X\times Y$ iff $1\in X$ and $2\in Y$ (then both are non-empty). Subsets of $A$ containing $1$: $2^{2}=4$; containing $2$: $2^{2}=4$. So $16$ products contain $(1,2)$. The empty set does not contain $(1,2)$.
originality_note: New: counting the subsets of AxA that are themselves Cartesian products X x Y, where the empty product is produced by many pairs (X,Y), with an excluded pair (way 5: Cartesian products linked with power-set counting). Closest known: 'number of relations from A to B = 2^(mn)' and 'n(P(A)xP(B))'. Different because: the map (X,Y) -> X x Y is not one-one, so the student must separate the empty case before counting.
blueprint_concepts: Cartesian product of sets; number of elements
Subsets, power set, number of subsets and proper subsets

concept_use.Cartesian product of sets; number of ele: n(XxY) = n(X)n(Y) shows the product is empty exactly when a factor is empty, and a non-empty product determines its factors.
concept_use.Subsets, power set, number of subsets an: Counting 2^3 - 1 = 7 non-empty subsets for each factor and 2^2 = 4 subsets containing a given element.

stem_review: Read as a student: every set, relation and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python by brute-force enumeration, is unique and equals the Answer Plan (positive 2-digit integer). Changed: moved the condition "(1,2) not in S" before "S = X x Y for some subsets X, Y" so that it cannot be read as a condition on X and Y.
key_step: Noticing that X x Y fixes X and Y only when both are non-empty, so the empty product must be counted once.
justification: Two ideas linked (injectivity of the product map except at the empty set, then complementary counting) with a numerical answer and a trap that changes the answer (counting 64 or 15+49). Comparable to 2026-P1-Q11 (L3) bounded counting.
